title: How many weeks?
summary: Work out how many weeks a goal takes, and track what's saved and what's left.

steps.title: Weeks to your goal
steps.body: Your goal counts only what's in Save. To find how many weeks it takes, see how many times your weekly saving fits into what's left. If it doesn't fit exactly, round up. The last bit still needs a whole week.
steps.example: A goal costs {m:2000}. You save {m:300} a week. After 6 weeks you have {m:1800}, still short. After 7 weeks you have {m:2100}. So it takes 7 weeks.

steps.prompt: Your goal costs {m:3000}. You start from zero and save {m:400} a week. How many weeks will it take?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. 7 weeks gives you {m:2800}. That's still {m:200} short, so you need one more week.
Not quite. That takes {m:400} away once. Count how many weeks of {m:400} you need.

steps.wrong: Not quite. See how many weeks of {m:400} it takes to reach {m:3000}.
hints: Count up in steps of {m:400}: {m:400}, {m:800}, {m:1200} and so on.
7 weeks gets you to {m:2800}. Is that enough?
steps.correct: That's it. 8 weeks. After 7 weeks you're {m:200} short, so you round up.

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. 8 weeks gives you {m:2400}. That's still {m:100} short, so you need one more week.
Not quite. That takes {m:300} away once. Count how many weeks of {m:300} you need.

replay.wrong: Not quite. See how many weeks of {m:300} it takes to reach {m:2500}.
hints: Count up in steps of {m:300}: {m:300}, {m:600}, {m:900} and so on.
8 weeks gets you to {m:2400}. Is that enough?
replay.correct: That's it. 9 weeks. After 8 weeks you're {m:100} short, so you round up.

steps.prompt: Your goal costs {m:4000}. You have {m:1500} in Save. How much is left to save?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That adds the two. Take what you've saved away from the price.
Not quite. That's what you've saved. How much more do you need?

steps.wrong: Not quite. Take what's in Save away from the price.
hints: What's left is the price minus what you've saved.
steps.correct: That's it. You've saved {m:1500}, and {m:2500} is left to go.

replay.wrong: Not quite. Take what's in Save away from the price.
hints: What's left is the price minus what you've saved.
replay.correct: That's it. You've saved {m:2000}, and {m:1500} is left to go.

steps.prompt: Which of these count toward your goal right now?

items.text: An allowance that's due but not handed over yet
A birthday gift that's now in Save
Money you've been told you'll get next month

steps.wrong: Not quite. Only money that's already in Save counts toward your goal.
hints: For each one, ask: is this money in Save right now?
Money that's due or promised hasn't reached Save yet. Spend isn't Save.
steps.correct: All sorted. Only money already in Save counts. Due, promised and Spend money don't count yet.

steps.prompt: Your goal costs {m:3000}. You already have {m:1000} in Save. You save {m:500} a week. How many more weeks?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That's counting from zero. You already have {m:1000}, so start from there.
Not quite. You need what's left after the {m:1000}, not the {m:1000} itself.

steps.wrong: Not quite. Work out what's left to save, then count the weeks.
hints: First take what you have away from the price.
{m:2000} is left. How many weeks of {m:500} is that?
steps.correct: That's it. {m:2000} is left, and 4 weeks of {m:500} covers it.

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That's counting from zero. You already have {m:600}, so start from there.
Not quite. You need what's left after the {m:600}, not the {m:600} itself.

replay.wrong: Not quite. Work out what's left to save, then count the weeks.
hints: First take what you have away from the price.
{m:1800} is left. How many weeks of {m:300} is that?
replay.correct: That's it. {m:1800} is left, and 6 weeks of {m:300} covers it.

steps.prompt: You're 5 weeks from your goal. You spend {m:600} from Spend. You keep saving the same each week. Does your goal take longer?

options.feedback: Not quite. Your goal counts Save, and you're still saving the same.
Not quite. Spending doesn't add anything to Save.

steps.outcome: Your goal counts what's in Save, and your weekly saving hasn't changed. Spending cash from Spend doesn't touch Save, so it's still 5 weeks.
hints: Which jar does your goal count?
The {m:600} came out of Spend, not Save.
steps.correct: Right. Spend and Save are separate. Your goal only counts Save.

steps.prompt: Why does saving {m:100} more each week get you to your goal sooner?

options.text: Each week adds more, so fewer weeks are needed

options.feedback: Not quite. The price stays the same. Your weekly amount is what changes.
Not quite. Only Save counts toward a goal.

hints: Does the price change, or what you put in each week?
Bigger steps reach the same place in fewer steps.
steps.correct: Right. Bigger weekly steps reach the same price in fewer weeks.
